clue.text: Work together with barrel-maker, brewing tea

indicators.note: tea that is brewing is being stewed and stirred, so its letters get mixed up

blocks.note: a cooper makes barrels
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cask-maker and a colleague collaborate over a pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-operate is to act jointly with others towards a shared aim.

clue.text: Award old vehicle claiming second

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the vehicle wraps round what follows

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for old
a car is a vehicle
abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A vintage car wins a prize for coming second.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for film achievement.

clue.text: Quietly mention favour

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to refer to something is to mention it

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly puts in a good word for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer something is to like it more, to favour it over alternatives.

clue.text: Barney maybe with bishops breaking law

indicators.note: something breaking into a thing splits it open and sits inside

blocks.note: a rule is a law
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone called Barney and some bishops are breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney Rubble is Fred Flintstone's neighbour in the cartoon The Flintstones; 'maybe' marks him as an example of someone bearing the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Barney is the best-known bearer of the surname, from the Flintstones cartoon, so he exemplifies a Rubble.

clue.text: Bird, an enormous creature

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is described as a huge beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one bird being enormous; the comma splits wordplay from definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods of Greek myth, so a titan is any huge being.

clue.text: Time before tea for a score at Wimbledon?

blocks.note: first meaning: half past three in the afternoon on the 24-hour clock, just before teatime
second meaning: a tennis score where server has one point and receiver two

explanation.surface: A schedule note at the tennis championships, where a match finishes before afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis tournament; tennis counts points as 15, 30, 40.
explanation.definitionFit: On the 24-hour clock 15:30 is mid-afternoon, and in tennis scoring it is a point-tally.

clue.text: Travelling a lot and running after the ball

indicators.note: one thing coming after another puts it second in the line

blocks.note: a globe is a ball, a sphere
trotting is running at an easy pace

explanation.surface: A footballer chases the ball all over the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Globetrotting means voyaging widely around the world, visiting many countries.

clue.text: Conflict on the football field or at a singing contest?

definitions.text: on the football field or at a singing contest?

blocks.note: first meaning: a fierce set battle between armies drawn up in position

blocks.clueFragment: on the football field or at a singing contest?
blocks.note: second meaning, punning: a fight on a pitch, or a contest of pitch between singers

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical reading: a pitch is a sports field and also the highness of a note.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitched battle is a planned, fully engaged clash, figuratively any intense struggle.

clue.text: Find out when sure

blocks.note: as in 'as he left' means when
certain means sure

explanation.surface: An instruction to discover things only once you are confident.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to establish or discover a fact for certain.

clue.text: Give another speech and study before shift

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: A speaker reviews notes before a change of plan and talks again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a change or a work period, but it is a loose dress; 'before' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-address an audience is to deliver a further address, or speech, to them.

clue.text: Woodland deity arranged stay by river

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A forest god has organised a stopover beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are half-goat forest spirits of Greek mythology, companions of Dionysus.

clue.text: Peer having no belief, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A lord who is an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'belief' is thinned out; 'no' stays whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is a noble, a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Role I will play in college

indicators.note: playing with something toys with it, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor announces the part they will take in a college production.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel College is an Oxford college, so it is an example of a college.

clue.text: British having departed, drink finally flowed and flowed

indicators.note: something that has departed has gone, so it is taken away
finally picks out the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: booze is alcoholic drink
B is the abbreviation for British, removed here
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: With the Brits gone, the drink poured freely.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'flowed' supplies only its last letter; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oozed means seeped or trickled out slowly, a sluggish kind of flowing.

clue.text: Popular seating area – messages found here?

blocks.note: fashionable things are in
a box is a private seating area in a theatre or stadium

explanation.surface: A fashionable stand at the ground, perhaps where notes are left.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a hint rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An inbox is where incoming emails or office mail collect awaiting attention.

clue.text: Document one might take from a letter

definitions.text: one might take from a letter

blocks.note: first meaning: a contract for renting property

blocks.clueFragment: one might take from a letter
blocks.note: second meaning: a letter here is someone who lets property, and tenants take this from them

explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like a written message or a character of the alphabet, but it means a landlord, one who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is the written agreement under which a tenant rents from an owner.

clue.text: Very unusual verse two at the end

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unexpected order
at the end picks the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A poem's second stanza is remarkably odd at its finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is an informal intensifier meaning extremely, as in 'ever so kind'.

clue.text: Former journalist goes round in high spirits

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one part wraps the other

blocks.note: ED is short for editor
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: An ex-reporter does the rounds in a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means joyful and exhilarated, a state of great happiness.

clue.text: Beastly type of crossing?

blocks.note: surface reading: a nasty sort of journey or an animal hybrid
setter's reading: a pedestrian crossing named after a striped African animal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' usually means horrid; here it means named after a beast. A British pedestrian crossing with black-and-white road stripes bears that animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped crossing takes its name from the horse-like African animal with black and white stripes.

clue.text: Rubbish match – Scots might consume this!

blocks.note: tat is cheap rubbishy goods
a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A poor game is watched by Scottish fans with a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Tattie is the Scots word for potato; a cup tie is a knockout match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattie is a potato in Scottish dialect, a staple Scottish food.

clue.text: Rescuer is initially lacking taste

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of the word before it
lacking something means being without it, so it is removed

blocks.note: a saviour rescues people
first letter of the word, removed here

explanation.surface: A lifeguard is first described as having no taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Savour as a noun is a characteristic flavour or smell; it also means to relish.

clue.text: Pot from New Orleans, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: a large metal cooking pot used by soldiers
second meaning: the American South, of which this city is one example

explanation.surface: A cooking pot brought back from a trip to Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: A dixie is British army slang for a camp kettle; Dixie is also the nickname of the southern US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixieland is the southern US, and New Orleans is a city there, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: In charge, step up to reach polar feature

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
a pace is a step

explanation.surface: The expedition leader urges a quicker stride to get to the North Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cap is a permanent sheet of ice covering polar land.

clue.text: Damage resulting from mischievous character leading broadcast

indicators.note: something leading goes in front, so it is placed first

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Harm caused by a troublemaker fronting a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or spoil something, making it worse.

clue.text: Some memorabilia curiously connected with Troy

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a portion of their letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Odd souvenirs from ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilium is the Latin name of Troy, giving the adjective; it also means relating to the hip bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Iliac means of Ilium, the ancient city of Troy, as in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Socialist bound by firm beliefs

definitions.note: plural clue word for a singular noun meaning a set of beliefs

indicators.note: something bound by another is tied inside it, enclosed

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A left-winger is held fast by strong convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective for beliefs but is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a statement of a person's guiding principles.

clue.text: Slashed one's skin

blocks.note: slashed means cut
one is I, and 's is S

explanation.surface: Someone has gashed their own skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the dermis and epidermis together.

clue.text: Hit on the head with old coin

blocks.note: first meaning: to strike someone on the skull
second meaning: a former British coin worth five shillings

explanation.surface: Someone is struck on the head with an antique piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is informally to hit their head, and the crown was a pre-decimal coin.

clue.text: Bend a rule and lengthen rally on court?

blocks.note: first meaning: to allow an exception beyond what is strictly permitted
second meaning, playful: prolong a tennis rally, which decides one point

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal tennis reading: a rally is played for a single point.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch a point is an idiom for going beyond the usual limits, making an allowance.

clue.text: One at baptism got to welcome padre possibly before noon

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several versions, so the letters may be rearranged
welcoming someone takes them in, so one part holds the other
before places one part ahead of the next

blocks.note: taken as written
the five letters rearranged
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A sponsor at a christening received the chaplain before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: A padre is a military chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent sponsors a child at its christening and promises to guide its faith.
